name: Opus 5 seasonality
strategy: A calendar-driven book sized off measured Jul-27-to-year-end window statistics computed over 2000-2025 daily history: overweight the sectors with the highest seasonal hit-rates into the Aug-Dec window (industrials, financials, regional banks, large-cap growth), hold gold and utilities as the measured Aug-Sep defensive/flow legs, short the two sleeves that most reliably lag the S&P over the same calendar window (developed non-US equity and intermediate Treasuries), and carry 7% cash as pre-committed dry powder for the Oct-1 and Nov-1 seasonal rotations.
novelty: The edge hypothesis is that returns are not distributed uniformly across the calendar: recurring institutional flows (fiscal-year and quarter-end rebalancing, the Halloween/best-six-months concentration of the equity risk premium in Nov-Apr, physical gold restocking into the Asian festival season, post-driving-season energy weakness, holiday retail build) leave measurable, repeating signatures in specific date windows, so position sizing should be a function of the date rather than of price trend or fundamentals. This is a genuinely different return driver from long-AI-momentum: the book is chosen by calendar-window hit-rate statistics, holds nothing for its growth story, is diversified across industrials/financials/gold/utilities/staples rather than concentrated in semis, and its shorts are index and duration sleeves rather than single-stock fades. It is falsified if the seasonal windows stop paying: specifically if Aug-Oct sees defensives (XLU/XLP/GLD) underperform while high-beta cyclicals lead, if EFA and IEF outperform SPY into year-end (they did so in only 9/24 and 5/23 past windows respectively), or if the Nov-Dec small/mid-cap seasonal lead fails to appear at the November reassessment.

positions.thesis: Large-cap growth leads the Aug-Oct calendar window: QQQ minus SPY over Jul-27 to Oct-31 averaged +1.05% with an 18/26-year (69%) hit rate, t=+1.35, and 8/10 in the last decade; QQQ absolute Jul-27 to Dec-31 averaged +3.97%, 20/26 years (77%). Held as the growth core through the Aug-Oct leg, to be trimmed toward mid/small caps at the November reassessment.

Highest-hit-rate sector in the window ahead. XLI Jul-27 to Dec-31 averaged +5.39% with a 21/26-year (81%) hit rate, t=+2.49, 9/10 in the last decade; the Nov-Dec leg alone (Oct-31 to Dec-31) averaged +4.68%, 21/26 years (81%), t=+3.78, and XLI minus SPY over Nov-Dec was +1.59%, 19/26 years (73%), t=+3.04.
Financials carry a strong Q4 seasonal: XLF Jul-27 to Dec-31 averaged +5.04%, 20/26 years (77%), and 9/10 in the last decade at an average +8.94%; Oct-31 to Dec-31 averaged +3.64%, 19/26 years (73%).

The Aug-Sep physical-gold restocking window is the cleanest non-equity seasonal I measured: GLD Jul-27 to Oct-27 averaged +3.54% with a 14/21-year (67%) hit rate, t=+1.69, and +3.36% average over the last 10 years; GLD minus SPY over the same window averaged +3.13%, 13/21 years, t=+1.80. Also the book's main equity-beta diversifier through the Aug-Sep tail-risk window.

Utilities are the one sector with a positive average through the weak stretch: XLU Jul-27 to Sep-30 averaged +1.14%, 18/26 years (69%) positive, versus SPY at -0.55%; XLU Sep-30 to Oct-31 averaged +1.24%, 19/26 years (73%), 8/10 in the last decade; XLU Jul-27 to Dec-31 averaged +4.47%, 19/26 years, t=+2.47.

Highest-return seasonal sleeve measured: KRE Jul-27 to Dec-31 averaged +7.24% with a 15/20-year (75%) hit rate, t=+2.28, and 8/10 in the last decade at +10.14% average; Oct-31 to Dec-31 alone averaged +5.91%, 15/20 years. Sized small and stopped at -25% because it is the highest-beta leg and the 2008 window ran -23.8%.

Highest t-statistic of any absolute sector window I measured: XLP Jul-27 to Dec-31 averaged +3.95%, 19/26 years (73%), t=+3.32; Oct-31 to Dec-31 averaged +2.87%, 20/26 years (77%), t=+3.93. Low-variance ballast for the Aug-Sep crash tail.

Developed non-US equity is the most reliable relative laggard into year-end: EFA minus SPY was positive in only 9/24 years (38%) over Jul-27 to Dec-31 and only 2/10 in the last decade at -2.65% average; over Jul-27 to Oct-31 it was positive in 10/24 years (42%), t=-1.33, and 2/10 in the last decade. Paired against QQQ this is the strongest spread I found: long QQQ / short EFA over Jul-27 to Oct-31 averaged +3.29%, 17/24 years (71%), t=+3.12.

The Halloween/best-six-months effect measured as a spread: intermediate Treasuries beat SPY in only 5/23 years (22%) over Jul-27 to Dec-31, and in only 1 of the last 10, average -6.00%. Chosen over higher-octane shorts (OIH, XOP, XLB) because it carries the highest hit rate at the lowest volatility and no squeeze risk; an earlier candidate book that shorted OIH was stopped out in both mandatory backtest windows.

historical_seasonal_study.method: Adjusted-close daily history 2000-01-03 to 2026-07-24 for 36 ETFs; for each candidate calendar window the return was computed year by year from the last close on or before the start date to the last close on or before the end date, and average / median / hit-rate / t-stat / worst case recorded. Composite-book returns use registered weights with 3% APR borrow on shorts and 4% APY on cash.
historical_seasonal_study.book_Jul27_to_Dec31: n=20 years, avg +3.87%, 17/20 (85%) positive, t=+2.38, worst -19.25% (2008); SPY same windows avg +3.90%, 19/26 (73%) positive, worst -27.08%. Book beat SPY in 7/20 years.
historical_seasonal_study.book_Jul27_to_Oct31: n=20 years, avg +1.45%, 15/20 (75%) positive, t=+1.23, worst -16.29%; SPY avg +0.73%, 17/26 (65%), worst -22.39%. Book beat SPY in 11/20 years.
historical_seasonal_study.effects_measured_but_not_traded_at_entry: BTC-USD Sep-30 to Oct-31 ('Uptober') avg +19.38%, 9/11 years (82%), t=+3.60, worst -7.24% — the single strongest statistic in the whole screen, but BTC's Jul-27 to Sep-30 window is 3/11 (27%) positive at -1.57% average, so it is deliberately NOT held at entry and is scheduled for the Oct-1 reassessment. Turn-of-the-month (SPY, buy close of last trading day minus 1, sell close of 3rd trading day of next month): 318 monthly windows since 2000, avg +0.263% per 4-day window, 57.2% hit, t=+2.23; those ~4 days per month compounded to +115% while the remaining ~17 days compounded to +277%, i.e. roughly 1.8x the per-day return. Not expressible in a buy-and-hold entry book; reserved for weekly reassessments.

backtest.notes: MULTIPLE TESTING IS THE MAIN CAVEAT AND I AM REPORTING SCREENED WINNERS. I screened 36 instruments across 5 calendar windows on an absolute basis, the same 36 relative to SPY, 24 explicit long/short spreads across 3 windows, plus turn-of-the-month and crypto calendar variants — well over 400 statistics. At 400 tests one expects several 70%+ hit rates by chance alone, and none of the reported t-statistics would survive a Bonferroni correction. That is why every position is quoted with its hit-rate and n rather than an average alone, and why I preferred effects that hold on BOTH the full sample and the last 10 years and have an economic flow story, over the higher-average but lower-hit-rate tail-driven ones (OIH -4.6% avg but only 36% hit; USO -9.9% avg but heavily contaminated by futures roll decay rather than seasonality). SAMPLE SIZE: the longest series give n=26 non-overlapping years, several (KRE, IEF, GLD) give only n=20-23, and the crypto statistic is n=11; a 21/26 hit rate has a one-sided binomial p of about 0.005 but is one observation per year, so the effective sample is tiny. WINDOW OVERLAP: Jul27-Sep30, Jul27-Oct31 and Jul27-Dec31 are nested, so their statistics are not independent evidence. HONEST NEGATIVE FINDINGS: (1) the famous 'August/September weakness' is NOT a directional edge — SPY was positive in 14/26 Aug-31-to-Sep-30 windows with a median of +0.30%; the negative -1.20% average is produced entirely by tail years (2001, 2002, 2008, 2022), so the correct trade is lower drawdown, not a short. (2) The seasonal window ahead is net POSITIVE (SPY Jul-27 to Dec-31 avg +3.90%, 19/26 years, t=+2.09), which is why this book is net long ~75% rather than market-neutral. (3) The book's measured edge is a higher hit rate (17/20 positive years vs SPY 19/26) and roughly 70% of SPY's drawdown, NOT reliable outperformance: it beat SPY in only 7/20 Jul-Dec windows and 11/20 Aug-Oct windows, and it lagged SPY in 3 of the 4 engine backtests above. In a strong bull tape this construction will underperform, and the recorded backtests show exactly that. ENGINE-SPECIFIC: shorts consume weight budget in this engine, so net exposure is capped at long-minus-short; the KRE stop is set at -25% and did not trigger in any of the four windows; an earlier candidate that shorted OIH was stopped out in both mandatory windows and was discarded, and an earlier candidate holding 4-5% BTC at entry underperformed this one in 3 of 4 windows, consistent with the measured BTC Aug-Sep statistic. All backtest figures above are verbatim from tracker/round2.py --backtest.

outlook: Base case is a mid-single-digit gain to year-end with materially smaller drawdowns than the index: the measured composite averaged +3.87% over Jul-27-to-Dec-31 in 17 of 20 past years with a worst case of -19.25% against SPY's -27.08%, so I expect to track near SPY with less pain rather than to beat it outright, and to lag if the tape runs hot. Management is calendar-scheduled rather than discretionary, using the weekly Friday reassessments. Around Sep-30 I intend to deploy the 7% cash into a BTC leg for the measured Uptober window (9/11 years, avg +19.4%, t=+3.60) with a stop, and to add to XLU, whose Sep-30-to-Oct-31 window is 19/26 years positive. Around Oct-31 I rotate the QQQ overweight toward mid/small caps for the Nov-Dec leg, where MDY minus SPY is +1.18% at t=+2.27 and IWM minus SPY is +1.42% at t=+1.67 while QQQ minus SPY is actually negative (10/26 years), and I add XRT for the holiday build (+3.80% avg, 13/20 years, and 7/10 in the last decade at +7.38%). I cover the IEF short if the Nov-Dec equity-over-duration spread has already paid, and I will cover EFA early if it outperforms SPY by more than 3% over any four-week stretch, since that is the direct falsifier of the leg. Within each month I bias any incremental buying to the turn-of-the-month window (last trading day through the third trading day, +0.263% average, 57% hit over 318 months) rather than mid-month. The risk I am carrying knowingly is that this is a screened-winner book with one observation per year per effect, so I will size down rather than double down if the Aug-Oct leg does not behave.
